newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products -Gulf gasoline gives back gains.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products -Gulf gasoline gives back gains.

text.p: U.S. Gulf conventional gasoline lost its strong momentum by late Friday, giving back all of a 1.25 cent differential gain reached earlier in the day as previously fervent buyers vanished from the market.

New York Harbor and Midcontinent conventional unleaded gasoline differentials were mostly higher by late day in sympathy with earlier Houston strength, while NYH reformulated grades firmed briskly on tight supply.
U.S. GULF
Gasoline trade quietly substantially by late Friday after differentials skyrocketed during early action, according to market players.

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline traded at 2.00 cents over August futures during morning activity, with talk emerging of other deals done as high as 2.25 cents over. But prices slipped off during the second half of the day to end about unchanged with Thursday's late levels between 0.50 and 0.75 cent over the August futures.

Traders attributed much of the strength to short covering by two major trade houses ahead of the scheduling deadline at the end of the day for the back 20th cycle on the Colonial Pipeline, the main artery from the Gulf to the East Coast.

The bullish tone for the week started at the scheduling deadline on Monday, when front 20th cycle M1 barrels leaped higher, according to traders. The conventional gasolines held the strength throughout the week, with differentials peaking at the early Friday highs.

The reasons behind Friday's differential rally were not entirely clear, but many players said two major trading houses were either forced to cover commitments or were attempting to drive prices higher to help a paper market position.
Estimates on the volume of regular conventional M1 that changed hands Friday sat between 250,000 and 500,00 barrels, though some players put the figure as high as 750,000 barrels.
Market watchers said that although the strength was largely due to the actions of a small number of players, tightness in prompt barrels may continue into next week.
"The way we've been moving the last few weeks I wouldn't be surprised to see this type of strength roll over into the 21st cycle (on the Colonial)," one gasoline trader said.
Any-month conventional M1 was seen near 1.50 cents under the August futures, near steady with its late Thursday levels.
Prompt reformulated gasoline A1 gasoline held its 4.50 cent-premium to the conventional, putting it about 5.50 cents over the August NYMEX at the end of Friday.
NEW YORK HARBOR:
NYH reformulted gasolines saw differentials spring to life in the afternoon, with "D2" grade 93-octane material sold for 8.75 cents over August futures -- about 1.25 cents firmer than Thursday diffs.
And "A2" reformulated 87-octane was offered at one cent over the print late day, 0.25 cent firmer than Thursday, with barrels exchanging hands for 0.85 cent over the screen Friday.
"Very few 'A2' cargoes are coming in," one trader said, adding that higher costs of gasoline additive MTBE were also helping expand reformulated diffs.
Conventional unleaded "M2" grade, meanwhile, was sold for 1.85 cents under August futures, a bit firmer than late Thursday diffs, with any-month material offered at 2.35 cents under.
On the distillate front, NYH prompt heating oil diffs were stable at 0.35 cent under the August print -- a bit firmer than Sun Co postings of 0.45 cent under.
And aviation-quality 54-grade jet fuel was offered at 1.75 cents over August NYMEX, a tad weaker than Thursday diffs.
MIDCONTINENT:

Midcontinent markets calmed down in afternoon trade after keen demand by refiners and traders pushed values higher in the morning. "The strength in the Gulf firmed Group Three gasoline," said one trader.

In light activity, Group Three prompt unleaded gasoline differentials held steady at about 3.25/3.50 cents over August futures, a quarter cent gain from Thursday. Any months were up about a half cent from Thursday, at 2.50/2.75 cents over the print.
Chicago prompt unleaded gasoline differentials weakened a quarter cent amid diminishing buyers at 2.50/2.75 cent. Any months were pegged 2.25/2.50 cents.
On the distillate side, Group Three prompt low sulphur diesel was largely steady from Thursday at 2.50/2.75 cents, with Chicago material a quarter cent stronger at about 0.25 cent below the print.
